title: Quarterly runway playbook: demand-weighted prioritization for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Produce a repeatable quarterly playbook that ranks hosted API endpoints and model candidates for the next release window using demand-weighted signals (traffic, revenue per token, customer SLAs, and runway risk), so we can allocate model-catalog commitments and Dedicated capacity with predictable SLOs and optimized unit costs.

Scope: Planning cadence and decision rules for hosted endpoints and model variants across the model catalog (curation, rotation, deprecation). Includes: data signals to use, scoring formula, acceptance gates, stakeholder signoff, rollout sequencing (canary -> staged), required observability dashboards, and post-release regression checks. Excludes on-prem-only private deployments (will follow a separate sync).

Approach:
1) Assemble normalized signals: 30-day active traffic, 90-day revenue proxy (usage * pricing tier), latency-sensitive route tags, and customer SLA tiers.
2) Compute a demand-weighted priority score combining traffic*revenue factor + SLA multiplier - volatility penalty (recent trend divergence).
3) Map top-priority models/endpoints to tranche lanes: Core (0-70% traffic), Reserve (70-95%), Contingency (95-100%).
4) For each tranche, define rollout velocity, canary windows, fallback model variants, and upgrade rollback triggers tied to Console SLO dashboards.
5) Tie recommendations to capacity commitments (Dedicated shards) and quantization/latency profiles via Optimize playbook.

Deliverables: playbook doc, scoring script (notebook + SQL), example prioritized list for Q2, Console dashboard mock, rollout checklist, exec one-pager for leadership signoff.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented scoring method with computed example list for all hosted routes; 2) Dashboard mock in Console with traffic and predicted SLO impact; 3) Engineering acceptance of rollout sequencing and rollback triggers; 4) Exec signoff on tranche thresholds and capacity commit recommendations; 5) Hand-off to Solutions & Sales with customer communication draft.
success_metrics: - Coverage: top 80% traffic mapped to Core/Reserve lanes by release window; - Prediction accuracy: <=10% deviation between predicted and observed traffic distribution in first 14 days; - SLO preservation: no more than 1 P1 incident attributable to model rollout in tranche windows; - Cost delta: show projected unit-cost improvement >=5% for recommended rotations/quantization in Reserve lane.
timeline: Mar 5 2026: kickoff and telemetry refresh; Mar 9: first scoring pass and top-50 list; Mar 16: cross-functional review (Eng/SRE/Design/Sales); Mar 23: final playbook and exec one-pager; Apr 1: runway-to-release handoff and canary scheduling; Apr 15: target tranche rollout begins.
risks:
- Telemetry gaps (route tagging inconsistent) could skew scores; mitigation: segment-level validation and conservative defaults.
- Capacity mismatch if Dedicated allocations not provisioned; mitigation: prebook reserve buffer and coordinate with Capacity team.
- Customer regressions from model swaps; mitigation: extended canaries for high-SLA customers and automatic rollback thresholds tied to quality eval hooks.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary small percentage (1-3%) on non-SLA routes for 48h with full tracing. 2) If canary passes health and regression checks, expand to Reserve lane (10-30%) for 72h. 3) Core lane migrations scheduled during low-latency windows with 2-hour rollback windows. 4) Automated fallback: route-level policy to fall back to previous model family when token-error-rate or response-latency breaches thresholds. 5) Post-rollout 14-day quality sweep tied to Redwood Optimize regression alerts.
